about.title: About
about.name: Lucas Rack
about.role: Electronics Engineer · Software, AI & Distributed Systems
about.summary: Electronics engineer with 5+ years of software experience across AI/LLM applications, distributed systems and enterprise data platforms. Currently building retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and machine-learning automation over Lenovo's global supply chain systems. Proficient in Python, Rust, SQL and PL/SQL.
about.contact_intro: Email is the fastest way to reach me. I also answer on LinkedIn.
about.education_thesis: End-to-end system for remote reading of household water meters. A battery-powered STM32L0 device counts the flow meter's pulses and reports daily over LTE-M/NB-IoT to a multi-node Rust head-end server, through a custom low-power protocol based on IEC 62056. I designed the device PCB in KiCad and characterized its power consumption on the bench, projecting over 8 years of battery life.

items.label: LLM & RAG systems
items.text: Built retrieval-augmented generation systems over internal supply chain documentation, so teams can query operational knowledge in natural language.

items.label: Production support
items.text: Provide level 2 support for production systems, diagnosing and resolving incidents to keep critical supply chain operations running.

items.label: ML automation
items.text: Automated manual workflows through machine-learning classification and data extraction, cutting processing time and human error across 24/7 global systems.

items.label: Embedded systems teaching
items.text: Guide students in designing, programming and debugging embedded C projects on STM32 (ARM Cortex-M), covering UART, SPI and I2C communication, interrupts, DMA, timers/PWM and ADC.

items.label: Rust development
items.text: Developed high-performance Rust applications for Ethereum Layer 1 and Layer 2 clients, improving transaction processing efficiency.

items.label: P2P protocols

items.label: Analysis and requirements
items.text: Performed functional and technical requirement analysis for Santander Global Tech projects, delivering optimized financial solutions.

items.label: SQL optimization

items.label: Python scripting

items.label: C/C++ firmware

items.label: Object-oriented programming
items.text: Taught C++ object-oriented programming and UML design in the Programming Laboratory course, for the Biomedical Engineering degree.

projects.name: IoT Head-End System
projects.description: A distributed head-end system for drinking-water telemetering, written in Rust. Clustering with SWIM failure detection, device delegation across nodes, a custom scheduler, persistence, and observability through Prometheus and Grafana. This is the software half of my capstone project, alongside the low-power firmware and the cellular PCB.
projects.image_alt: 3D render of the meter board, showing the cellular module and the microcontroller

projects.name: DS2000
projects.description: A USB button box for Discord, built end to end: a Rust desktop application with Tauri, C++ firmware on the microcontroller, and a custom PCB designed in KiCad. Mute, deafen and disconnect from a physical button, with RGB LEDs mirroring the state.
projects.image_alt: Front view of the DS2000 button box

projects.name: mechardo3d.xyz
projects.description: This very site: a Rust server on Axum, with Tera templates and Tailwind, and no framework JavaScript. Bilingual with language detection, a sitemap generated from the routing table, a rate-limited contact form, and a Docker deployment behind Caddy.

projects.name: IoT alarm over MQTT
projects.description: A connected home alarm: an ESP32 running ESPHome watches the motion, door and doorbell sensors, publishes events to an MQTT broker, and a bridge written in Rust forwards them to Telegram. Real-time alerts on hardware that was already installed.
projects.image_alt: Inside of the alarm enclosure, showing the ESP32 and the relays

projects.name: Motorcycle on-board computer
projects.description: An on-board computer for a motorcycle built on ARM Cortex-M3, with two OLED screens, GPS and Bluetooth connectivity. An embedded system designed to read, process and display vehicle telemetry while riding.
projects.image_alt: On-board computer mounted on a motorcycle dashboard

projects.name: Wilson the quadruped
projects.description: A quadruped robot on Arduino, programmed entirely in AVR Assembly. Gait control and servo driving written by hand, with no libraries in between: an exercise in low-level programming and hardware control.
projects.image_alt: The Wilson quadruped robot assembled on a workbench

projects.name: Portal
projects.description: An online multiplayer game inspired by Portal, written in C++ with SDL and Qt. A client-server architecture over sockets and threads, with its own level editor and real-time physics simulation.
projects.image_alt: Screenshot of a Portal game session

projects.name: Al-Go-Oh!
projects.description: A card game based on Yu-Gi-Oh!, written in Java with a JavaFX interface. A large exercise in object-oriented design: the rules of the game modelled with design patterns and covered by tests.
projects.image_alt: Board of the Al-Go-Oh! card game
